cues: Branching lowers the boiling point, since a compact molecule has less surface contact.
The small alcohols mix with water in all proportions, because they hydrogen bond with it, but solubility falls as the oily carbon chain grows.
Alcohols are less dense than water, and such weak acids that they do not affect litmus.
